summary: In Japan, keeping and hobby-breeding a captive-bred roof rat is legal and unregulated federally: the species is deliberately NOT a 'Specified Animal' (特定動物, hazardous) and NOT a 'Designated Invasive Alien Species' (特定外来生物), a 2005 expert committee chose to exclude it because it's too long-established to regulate. Commercial activity (breeding for profit, retail sale, exhibition, or large-scale free rehoming) triggers registration as a First-Class (or Second-Class) Animal Handling Business with facility/welfare standards. The big restriction is IMPORT: bringing a roof rat into Japan is de-facto prohibited for the public, the Ministry of Health requires imported rodents to have lived since birth in a foreign-government-designated biosecure facility (homes/hobby breeders don't qualify). Never release one.

keep.why: Private possession needs no federal permit: R. rattus is not a 'Specified Animal' (特定動物, that list targets primates, big carnivores, large/venomous reptiles, not rodents), and it is not a 'Designated Invasive Alien Species' (特定外来生物). The 2005 Ministry of the Environment expert committee deliberately excluded it (long-established via maritime trade; eradication-vs-pet distinction). Domestic keeping is treated like keeping a fancy rat or guinea pig.
keep.governing_law: Act on Welfare and Management of Animals (動物愛護管理法); Invasive Alien Species Act (外来生物法), R. rattus not listed; Specified Animal list (rodents excluded).

breed.why: Private breeding without intent to profit/advertise/distribute commercially is entirely outside the commercial animal-handling law. (Commercial-scale breeding triggers First-Class Animal Handling Business registration, see sell_give.)
breed.governing_law: Act on Welfare and Management of Animals (動物愛護管理法).

sell_give.why: Selling for profit (or breeding to sell) requires registration as a First-Class Animal Handling Business (第一種動物取扱業) with the prefecture, plus facility/caging/disclosure standards and an Animal Handling Manager. Giving animals away free to 'a large number of unspecified people' on a continuing basis requires Second-Class (第二種) notification. Occasional free rehoming to friends/family is unregulated.
sell_give.governing_law: Act on Welfare and Management of Animals, First-Class (第一種) & Second-Class (第二種) Animal Handling Business registration.

transport.why: DOMESTIC transport between prefectures is unregulated (subject only to carrier policies). IMPORT is de-facto prohibited for pets: under the Infectious Diseases Control Law's Animal Import Notification System, all live rodents need a health certificate from the EXPORTING government certifying the animal lived since birth in a government-designated disease-free facility, which homes and hobby breeders cannot obtain, so a pet roof rat cannot legally be imported. (R. rattus is not on the absolute-prohibition list, but the facility rule is an effective ban.) Export from Japan is legal with the destination country's health certificate (MAFF AQS). Never release.
transport.governing_law: Act on the Prevention of Infectious Diseases (感染症法), Animal Import Notification System (MHLW); Domestic Animal Infectious Diseases Control Law (MAFF AQS) for export.

restrictions.summary: Commercial selling/breeding (for profit) = First-Class Animal Handling Business registration (第一種動物取扱業) with the prefecture: facility floor plans, cleanable escape-resistant enclosures, space to 'stand/lie/move' naturally, an Animal Handling Manager, and written species/sex/origin disclosure at transfer. Large-scale non-commercial giveaway = Second-Class (第二種) notification (penalty up to ¥300,000 for failing to notify).
steps: Register as a First-Class Animal Handling Business before any commercial sale/breeding
Or file a Second-Class notification for large-scale free rehoming
restrictions.where_to_file: Prefectural government (animal welfare center / public health dept)

restrictions.summary: Importing a roof rat into Japan is effectively impossible for pet owners: imported rodents need an exporting-government health certificate proving the animal lived since birth in a government-DESIGNATED biosecure facility (homes/hobby breeders can't qualify). MHLW states such pets 'basically cannot be brought into Japan.'
restrictions.where_to_file: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (quarantine station at port of entry)
